subject.title: CLAW-526: Gate public publishes without breaking old CLIs

question: Should ClawHub adopt this exact TruffleHog-plus-ClawScan publication policy, including publishing ClawScan-suspicious artifacts and deleting secret-positive pending uploads, once the missing spec and live proof are added?
rationale: The diff changes which scanner controls public availability and how suspicious, malicious, and secret-positive uploads are retained or deleted; tests cannot determine the intended permanent security policy.

options.title: Approve policy after proof
options.body: Confirm the proposed verdict mapping, require the specification and redacted preview proof, then merge with the production flag disabled until deployment verification.

options.title: Keep suspicious private
options.body: Require suspicious ClawScan results to remain non-public pending moderation, then update tests, CLI status, and specifications to match.

options.title: Retain current scanner chain
options.body: Do not replace the existing Codex and SkillSpector path until a separately approved scanner migration and comparison plan exists.

recommendation.title: Approve policy after proof
recommendation.body: Confirm the proposed verdict mapping, require the specification and redacted preview proof, then merge with the production flag disabled until deployment verification.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is the credited introduction of the existing publication-quarantine boundary.
